title: Restriction-zero sections are killed by a power of an invertible section
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $X_s=\{x\in X:s(x)\ne0\text{ in }\mathcal L_x\otimes\kappa(x)\}$, where $\kappa(x)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. If $t\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ restricts to zero on $X_s$, then there exists $m\ge0$ such that the image of $t$ under multiplication by $s^{\otimes m}$ is zero in $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$.
